common_name: Delightful Garnet Coneflower (Compact Fragrant Ruby-Red Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Garnet is a 2025 introduction in Terra Nova Nurseries' compact Delightful coneflower series, bred primarily for pot and patio culture.

directions: Delightful Garnet is a dwarf coneflower bred for container and patio culture, forming a tidy, bowl-shaped mound only about 8 inches tall with flower stems reaching 14 inches. Its bright ruby-garnet blooms are noticeably fragrant, an unusual trait for Echinacea, and open continuously from June through October. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil; the plant is fast-growing, deer-resistant, and draws bees, butterflies, and other pollinators over an unusually long season for such a compact selection.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Delightful series, new for 2025)

common_name: Delightful Sunshine Coneflower (Compact Fragrant Yellow Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in average, coarse, well-drained soil in full sun; Sunshine is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the compact Delightful coneflower series.

directions: Delightful Sunshine carries extremely bright, sunny-yellow flowers over deep emerald-green foliage on a compact, vigorous mound only 9 inches tall with flowers rising to about 15 inches. Like its series-mates it is fragrant, blooming from June through October and drawing bees, hummingbirds, and butterflies over a long season. Grow in full sun in average soil, ideally coarse and slightly mineral, and expect a fast-growing, deer-resistant plant well suited to containers, beds, and borders alike.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Delightful series, new for 2025)

common_name: Delightful Tropics Coneflower (Compact Double Orange-Mango Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Tropics is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the compact Delightful coneflower series, notable for fully double blooms.

directions: Delightful Tropics produces fully double, sweetly scented blooms described by the breeder as a blend of orange, mango, and ruby grapefruit, holding their color well over a long June-to-October bloom season. It forms a compact, mounding, fast-growing plant about 12 inches tall with flower stems to 16 inches, bred primarily for pot and patio culture but equally at home in a sunny border. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil; it is deer-resistant and attracts bees, hummingbirds, and butterflies throughout its bloom period.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Delightful series, new for 2025)

common_name: Delightful Prosecco Coneflower (Compact Double Golden-Yellow Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Prosecco is a 2026 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the compact Delightful coneflower series, with fully double golden-yellow pompom flowers.

directions: Delightful Prosecco bears double, golden pompom flowers that the breeder describes as fizzy sunshine on sturdy stems, blooming continuously and heavily from June into October without any pinching required. Its clumping, fast-growing habit stays compact at roughly 14 to 16 inches, and it is noted as fragrant and suitable even for hot, humid Deep South gardens. Grow in full sun in average soil, ideally coarse and slightly mineral, allowing the soil to dry moderately between waterings; it is deer-resistant and draws hummingbirds and pollinators throughout its long bloom window.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Delightful series, new for 2026)

common_name: Summer Sienna Sweet Coneflower (Tawny Sun-Bronzed Rudbeckia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in average, well-drained to moist soil in full sun; Summer Sienna is a 2024 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction (US Plant Patent PP37,162) bred for tawny, sun-bronzed flower color.

directions: Summer Sienna produces mid-sized, tawny, sun-bronzed orange flowers in unusually heavy numbers from midsummer through fall, on an upright, clumping, fast-growing plant with flower stems reaching about 30 inches above a 16-inch foliage mound. Its informal, warm-toned color sets it apart from the straight-yellow sweet coneflowers already common in cultivation, and its abundant bloom makes it a strong cut flower as well as a pollinator magnet for bees and butterflies. Grow in full sun in average, moist to well-drained soil; the breeder's own hardiness rating runs zones 8 to 10, so gardeners in colder zones should treat it cautiously until wider trialing confirms performance.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (new for 2024)

common_name: White Feather Blazing Star (Compact First-Year-Flowering White Liatris)

planting.note: Plant corms or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; White Feather is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction (US Plant Patent PP37,556) bred for a more robust habit than older white blazing star selections.

directions: White Feather is a white-flowered blazing star bred to flower in its first year, with the breeder calling it the best habit of any Liatris they have produced, forming a fast, robust, 10-inch clump with flower spikes rising to about 18 inches. Like other Liatris it emerges late in spring, staying underground until the weather is reliably warm, then blooms from August into October, later than most perennials in the border. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil; it is deer-resistant, drought-tolerant once established, and strongly attracts pollinators and hummingbirds, making a good cut flower as well as a garden plant.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (new for 2025)

common_name: Nova Amber Threadleaf Coreopsis (Compact Mildew-Resistant Amber-Orange Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Amber is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the mildew-resistant Nova threadleaf coreopsis series.

directions: Nova Amber bears cheery, amber-orange flowers against deep green, slender, threadleaf foliage on an extremely dense, bushy, mounding plant that spreads wider than it is tall. It blooms heavily from June through September and is bred for improved mildew resistance compared with older threadleaf coreopsis cultivars. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil; it is drought-tolerant once established, deer-resistant, and attracts bees and hummingbirds, performing well in beds, borders, mass plantings, or containers.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Nova series, new for 2025)

common_name: Nova Opal Threadleaf Coreopsis (Compact Whisper-Pink Coral-Eyed Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Opal is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the mildew-resistant Nova threadleaf coreopsis series.

directions: Nova Opal covers itself abundantly in whisper-pink flowers with a small coral eye, a soft pastel departure from the yellow and orange tones typical of threadleaf coreopsis. The low, mounding, fast-growing plant keeps its finely cut foliage mildew-free late into the season and blooms from June through October. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil, allowing it to dry moderately between waterings; it is deer-resistant, low-water once established, and a reliable pollinator draw for beds, borders, and containers alike.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Nova series, new for 2025)

common_name: Nova Sunstone Threadleaf Coreopsis (Compact Rusty Peach-to-Pink Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Sunstone is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the mildew-resistant Nova threadleaf coreopsis series, a standout from the breeder's 2023 trials.

directions: Nova Sunstone offers unusual rusty peach-to-sun-tanned-pink flowers that cover a vigorous, fast-growing, mounding plant from June through October. It was a standout performer in the breeder's own trial gardens before release and keeps the fine, threadleaf foliage typical of this mildew-resistant series. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil; it is deer-resistant, needs little water once established, and draws a steady stream of pollinators through its long bloom season.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Nova series, new for 2025)

common_name: Sunny Days Rays Coreopsis (Color-Shifting Lemon-to-Coral Tickseed)
scientific_name: Coreopsis verticillata 'Sunny Days Rays' (Sunny Days series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Rays is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction bred from mildew-resistant threadleaf coreopsis lineage.

directions: Sunny Days Rays opens bright lemon-gold and shifts through tawny orange to blushing pink and coral as each flower ages, so a single dense, bushy plant displays several autumn-toned colors at once. Its fine, needle-like foliage stays mildew-resistant thanks to its threadleaf breeding, and it blooms heavily from June through September. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil, letting it dry moderately between waterings; it is deer-resistant and especially attractive to honeybees, suiting mixed beds, borders, mass plantings, or containers.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Sunny Days series, new for 2025)

common_name: Sunstar Gold Threadleaf Coreopsis (Gold Red-Eyed Mildew-Resistant Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Gold is a 2024 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the mildew-resistant Sunstar threadleaf coreopsis series.

directions: Sunstar Gold bears gold, red-eyed flowers over feathery, mildew-resistant foliage, holding a clean, manicured habit through an extremely long bloom time from June into September. It is a compact, well-behaved threadleaf coreopsis bred for garden performance as much as flower color. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil; it is deer-resistant and a dependable pollinator attractor, working well in mixed beds, borders, mass plantings, or containers.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Sunstar series, new for 2024)
